children: , the hybrid-cloud and quantum-computing giant, secured a finalized $1 billion Commerce Department award for its Anderon subsidiary Wednesday. IBM shares gained approximately 0.2% to $237.87 Thursday morning.

Anderon is operating a 300-millimeter quantum-wafer foundry in Albany, New York, giving IBM a manufacturing foothold deeper in the quantum supply chain. IBM is putting another $1 billion of its own capital behind the project, while initial wafers have already entered production. The facility is designed to manufacture technology for superconducting qubits, input-output signaling and readout components, with additional quantum architectures expected to follow.

The funding math is important. The federal government is providing $1 billion against the $2 billion of newly disclosed commitments, reducing how much IBM must fund itself while potentially turning Anderon into manufacturing infrastructure for outside quantum-chip designers. The valuation picture is also relatively restrained: IBM's $237.87 share price sits about 2% below its $242.72 GF Value estimate. The bigger unknown is commercialization, because IBM has not disclosed customers, purchase commitments, wafer volumes or expected Anderon revenue yet.

title: IBM Secures $1 Billion Commerce Award as Quantum Foundry Starts Production
